note: Every key and credential here is a fixed TEST value that protects nothing. Run each vector with a fresh replay store seeded with replay.seen_jtis (or one that always fails when replay.store is "unavailable"), at the Unix time `now`.

vectors.description: A GET with no query and no body: no qsh, no bdh. att.role is absent, so the ambient key signed.
A POST with a query and a JSON body: qsh and bdh are the hex SHA-256 of the raw query and body bytes.
pth is the path exactly as sent, percent-encoding included, without the query.
A request URL ending in a bare `?` has no query: the signature carries no qsh.
att.role = "user_present": the user-present key signed; the identity's role says so.
The attestation is signed EdDSA, with a kid.
The attestation is signed RS256, with a kid.
iat is 20 s in the future: within the 30 s tolerance.
att carries application attributes beside status; they are surfaced, not interpreted.
Only the attestation: it is public, so alone it is a bearer token.
Only the signature: an anonymous key.
An empty header is an absent credential, not a malformed one.
The attestation is not a compact JWS.
att is a key-role string instead of an object (the shape profile v1 retires).
status sits at the top level and att is missing (the shape profile v1 retires).
The attestation says alg none.
The request signature uses a symmetric algorithm.
The device signs RS256: profile v1 allows RS256 for issuers only.
The attestation names an issuer the verifier does not trust.
The attestation's kid is not in the issuer's JWKS.
The attestation header has no kid: profile v1 requires one.
The attestation claims a trusted kid but another key signed it.
The attestation expired an hour ago.
att.status is "suspended".
att has no status: fail closed.
THE critical case: the victim's genuine attestation with a request genuinely signed by the attacker's own key. Both signatures verify; only the thumbprint check refuses.
The embedded jwk carries a private member d.
The signature header has no jwk.
The claims were changed after signing (another jti), the signature kept.
exp passed 90 s ago, beyond the 30 s tolerance.
iat is 120 s ahead, beyond the 30 s tolerance.
exp - iat is one hour: profile v1 allows 300 s.
Signed for DELETE, sent as GET.
Signed for /accounts/1, sent to /accounts/2.
Signed for another API.
The query was changed after signing.
The request has a query but the signature has no qsh.
The signature has a qsh but the request has no query: the query was stripped.
The body was changed after signing.
The request has a body but the signature has no bdh.
The signature has a bdh but the request has no body: the body was stripped, so a signed write would replay as an empty one.
The jti was already used.
The replay store cannot be reached: fail closed, exactly like a replay.
OPTIONAL: the device key is Ed25519 (EdDSA). Clients sign ES256; a verifier MAY accept EdDSA device keys.
